I'm pretty divided on the gun control issue, honestly I can't really form an opinion. Raised in a semi-rural area where hunting was a big part of the culture. I respect the arguments from both sides, but I really think simplifying it to "no guns" or "guns" or "some guns" mitigates the complexity of the issue, it's going to be a multi-faceted solution, though in all fairness I have no idea what that looks like.

My only issue is I really don't understand the strict adherence to the Constitution. It's a beautiful document but when the founding fathers wrote it, they couldn't have possibly fathomed what "arms" would look like today. We added the banning of alcohol into the Bill of Rights for a long time, then took it out. The litigation of the Constitution isn't sacred, it's the values and philosophy. Making things binary decisions really just insults our own intelligence, multi-causal problems require complex solutions. Just my two cents :)

It is adherence to the bill of rights that is still active today. It is a living document and has been ratified numerous times. If we really have entered an age where the people believe arms have gotten too dangerous and must be stopped then an amendment needs to be proposed and ratified.

Ultimately though arms I believe is only used to mean a handheld weapon. No one is suggesting howitzers should be legal for citizens. The people have given a ton of ground in this area away to government already. Automatic weapons, stock configuration, and barrel length are banned/controlled nationally. Also, magazine size and much more is controlled in certain states.

Here's the bottom line: it is plainly written in the Constitution that our right to bear arm shall not be infringed, NOT so that we can go hunting or have "target practice", but so that a militia can be maintained and properly trained.

The second amendment exists so that we can protect ourselves from tyranny. Everything else is a bonus.
